acceptance.given: During each external process execution initiated by the toolchain evaluator, the process executor applies a configured finite output limit.

oracle.expected: Execution evidence shows output remains within the configured finite limit, with deterministic truncation or bounded failure when exceeded.
forbidden: An external process produces output without a bound.
oracle.observable: A process-execution test report records the configured output bound and observed bounded output or bounded failure.

acceptance.then: The output-bound check passes only when observed output remains within the configured finite limit.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the process-executor output-limit test with an over-limit output fixture; it must fail when no finite output bound is enforced.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce a finite output bound for every toolchain external-process execution, with deterministic truncation or bounded failure when exceeded.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the existing process-executor interface while enforcing the finite output bound.

slice_hint.state_transition: unbounded output -> bounded output with deterministic terminal handling
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The invocation records a finite output limit and terminates with output at or below that limit or a deterministic bounded failure.

acceptance.given: During each external process execution initiated by the toolchain evaluator, the process executor applies a configured finite time limit.

oracle.expected: Execution evidence shows the process terminates or is stopped at or before the configured finite timeout with a deterministic terminal state.
forbidden: An external process runs without a time bound.
oracle.observable: A process-execution test report records the configured timeout and observed termination or bounded stop.

acceptance.then: The time-bound check passes only when the process terminates or is stopped within the configured finite limit.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the process-executor timeout test with a blocking process fixture; it must fail when no finite timeout stops the process.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce a finite timeout for every toolchain external-process execution and produce a deterministic stopped or terminated state on expiry.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the existing process-executor interface while enforcing finite timeout behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: unbounded duration -> finite timeout with deterministic termination
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The invocation records a finite timeout and reaches a terminal result no later than that timeout, including deterministic timeout-stop status when needed.

acceptance.given: During validator evaluation, the semantic-dependency graph and declared dependency edges are available for inspection.

oracle.expected: A dedicated validator computes semantic-dependency closure and emits independent evidence that every required dependency is reachable.
forbidden: Semantic-dependency closure verification is omitted or inferred solely from another verification.
oracle.observable: A closure-validation report contains the graph input, closure computation, and an explicit pass/fail result.

acceptance.then: Semantic-dependency closure is independently verified and evidence is bound to this obligation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the dedicated closure validator against a graph with a missing reachable dependency; it must fail on the closure defect.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Compute and validate semantic-dependency closure independently, including detection of missing dependency edges.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain existing semantic context schema and validator interfaces while adding independent closure evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: closure not independently verified -> computed closure with dedicated evidence
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The closure validator succeeds only when all declared semantic dependencies are transitively reachable and independent evidence is emitted.

acceptance.given: The evaluation-seed manifest contains records for the three named evaluation seeds and their provenance fields.

oracle.expected: Validation finds exactly one occurrence for each named seed and verifies provenance, applicability, missing labels, counterexample or explicit absence, and approved non-baseline classification.
forbidden: Any named evaluation seed occurs zero times.
Any named evaluation seed occurs more than once.
oracle.observable: A parsed manifest report lists all three named seed identifiers with count 1 and valid required metadata.

acceptance.then: The manifest is accepted only when each named seed occurs exactly once with complete required metadata.
acceptance.when: When evaluation seeds are recorded or evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the seed-manifest validator against a fixture with a duplicate or missing named seed; it must fail the exact-once cardinality and metadata check.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate the three named evaluation seeds for exact-one cardinality and all required FR-6 provenance and classification fields.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing manifest fields and schema compatibility while rejecting missing or duplicate named seeds.

slice_hint.state_transition: unspecified seed occurrence -> exactly one validated record per named seed
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validation succeeds only when all three named seed identifiers occur exactly once and every required FR-6 metadata field is present and valid.
